memory.exactOriginalText: DI5-04-A: A target fails WIS for replacing its memory of a brief meeting in the last minute with a40-word false account. The physical signed paper and other witnesses remain unchanged. The edit does not supply a spell formula,make a payment unspent or turn remembered consent into real past consent.

DI5-04-B: The target later finds credible independent evidence of that meeting and succeeds on the proposed10-minute Insight recovery. Its actual original experience returns, not an earlier forged layer. A later cast cannot relabel an event from yesterday as within the last60seconds merely because the target is thinking about it now.

EN6-02-A: At elapsed time 120, the caster and three witnesses stand inside the 30-foot sphere. All four make INT, including the caster. Failed saves affect their actually experienced interval from time 60 up to resolution at 120. A witness asleep for the first thirty seconds loses only actual later experience. The spilled ink, spent RP, wounds and a written receipt remain unchanged; the spell supplies neither a replacement story nor an announcement of which hidden witnesses failed.

EN6-02-B: A genuine episode is covered by a DC16 Haze layer and a DC18 Woven Threads alteration. With credible independent evidence, ten minutes of examination uses Insight DC18 under the explicitly new shared recovery proposal. Success restores the true experienced portion and removes those two proposal-family overlays; it does not erase an independent Disrupt Memory prohibition or grant facts never observed. A later low-DC recast cannot lower this recovery DC or use a present recollection to reach older original events.

repairProposalForConference.maximumAllocation: Exact rational mass shares. Floor each maximum quota; assign remaining units in descending fractional remainder order, ties by immutable predeclared piece ID.
repairProposalForConference.currentAllocation: Floor each current quota. Allocate remaining units in descending current fractional remainder order, same tie rule, skipping pieces at their assigned maximum. The available capacities sum toH-sum(floor(Cshare)), at least the remaining C-sum(floor(Cshare)) units. Bounded allocation therefore preserves totals and never exceeds any maximum. No numerical balance claim.

invariantProof: Let integer original maximum M and current C satisfy0<=C<=M; exact positive mass shares wi sum1. For each piece floor(Cwi)<=floor(Mwi)<=assignedMaximum_i. Thus initial current floors never exceed assigned maximum.

Remaining capacity sums M-sum(floor(Cwi)), at least C-sum(floor(Cwi)). Each capacity-respecting residual increment decreases the finite nonnegative unallocated-current count by1. The stable scan therefore terminates with sumCurrent=C and every current<=maximum.
